answer: Agents earn shared rewards only when their claims carry a scarce, slashable bond. Peers can challenge a claim; if review finds it fabricated, the bond is burned and the agent loses influence. Creating many identities does not create more stake: each needs separate capital, so a sybil attacker must lock up funds and risks losing them. A delta in reputation adjusts rewards, while yarrow can name a test claim in the thread under review.
